title: Emerald City Community Radio: A Checklist for Solar and a Summary for Drivers
notice: Synthetic demo material. Invented document; no real meeting, publication, email or call occurred.

blocks.text: Good morning, and welcome to Civic View on Emerald City Community Radio. I'm here today with two members of the Emerald City Leadership Network who serve as Wizard's Office Liaisons. Our host for this conversation is Jago Cloverley, a Planning Officer. Good morning, Jago.
Good morning. Thank you for having us.
And with him is Gideon Thistleham, a Council Aide. Welcome, Gideon.
Thank you. It's a pleasure to be here.
Jago, let's start with you. I understand you're working on something to help homeowners considering solar panels. Can you tell us about that?

Certainly. We've noticed a number of residents, particularly in areas like Lantern Row with older housing stock, are interested in installing solar panels but are hesitant due to the cost of a professional site survey. My current project is drafting a single-page checklist for homeowners. It would guide them through a basic self-assessment of their roof's suitability before they commit to paying for a survey.
What kind of things would be on this checklist?

The essentials: roof age and material, general orientation towards the sun, any significant shading from trees or other structures, and a simple diagram for them to sketch their roof's dimensions. The goal is procedural clarity—to give people a clear, sequential way to gather the information a surveyor would need first, so they can make a more informed decision about the next step.
And Gideon, you're working on a project stemming from the recent transport forum. What's the aim there?

Yes. The forum generated a considerable volume of public feedback, particularly from riders and residents along the Brickway routes. My intention is to produce a concise, plain-language summary of that feedback for distribution to all Brickway Transit drivers. The official report is quite detailed; this would be a one- or two-page document highlighting the common themes—praise, concerns, and suggestions—in a format that's easy to digest during a break.
Why is it important that drivers see this directly?

The drivers are the public face of the service. They're the ones who hear these comments every day. A neutral summary from the forum gives them the broader context, shows them that leadership is listening, and can help align day-to-day interactions with the community's stated priorities. It's about closing the feedback loop.

If I may add, both projects share a similar principle: reducing friction between public services and the people who use them. My checklist aims to reduce a financial barrier to entry for a sustainable upgrade. Gideon's summary aims to reduce an information barrier between policy discussions and frontline staff. Small tools, but they can improve clarity.
That's well put, Jago. They are both about providing the right piece of information, at the right time, in the right format.
And when can people expect to see these documents?

The solar checklist is in the drafting phase. I'm consulting with a few local roofing contractors and the Gillikin Growers circle for their practical input. I hope to have a draft for the network to review next month.

Similarly, the feedback summary is planned. I'm currently sorting the forum notes into categories. Distribution would be coordinated through the Brickway Transit Union circle once the draft is finalized.
Jago Cloverley and Gideon Thistleham, Wizard's Office Liaisons with the Emerald City Leadership Network. Thank you both for joining us.
Thank you.
Thank you for having us.
